land.text: the Ordos and the bend of the Yellow River in northern Shaanxi and western Inner Mongolia: Cliopatria's Sui 626 shape, which is Liang Shidu's holding

predecessors.note: 'In or shortly before 617' Liang Shidu returned to his home commandery, Shuofang, and 'declared a state of Liang and himself its emperor' (Liang Shidu page); the Transition page has his Liang 'by 617'.

land.text: the Ordos and the bend of the Yellow River in northern Shaanxi and western Inner Mongolia: Cliopatria's Sui 626 shape, which is Liang Shidu's holding

successors.note: Under Tang siege in 628 his cousin Liang Luoren killed him and surrendered; the page gives 28 May 628 (Old Book of Tang) or 3 June 628 (New Book of Tang).

capitals.name: Shuofang (Yulin)
capitals.note: The page: Xia Province, 'roughly modern Yulin', had become Shuofang Commandery; 'the eastern city of Liang's capital Shuofang' fell to the Tang in spring 622. Coordinates are Yulin, Shaanxi, the researcher's reading.

rulers.name: Liang Shidu
rulers.note: Emperor of Liang, era Yonglong; infobox reign 617-628.

correction.text: the Ordos and the bend of the Yellow River in northern Shaanxi and western Inner Mongolia: Cliopatria's Sui 626 shape, which is Liang Shidu's holding

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 617-628 for a state Cliopatria lacks (Cliopatria files it as 'Sui Dynasty' 626-627, 109,171 km2; Cliopatria's Sui 617 shape already omits it): 'retained the modern northern Shaanxi and western Inner Mongolia region for over a decade'. No area on the page.

region.text: the Ordos and the bend of the Yellow River in northern Shaanxi and western Inner Mongolia: Cliopatria's Sui 626 shape, which is Liang Shidu's holding

ledger.note: 617: Liang Shidu rises at Shuofang. 'In or shortly before 617, he quit the army and returned to his home commandery'; he 'declared a state of Liang and himself its emperor' (era Yonglong; infobox 617-628). The page gives no date for the imperial title.

region.text: the eastern city of Shuofang, near modern Yulin

ledger.note: 622: the Tang take the eastern city of Shuofang. 'Tang forces took the eastern city in spring 622, forcing Liang back to the western city.'

region.text: the Ordos and the bend of the Yellow River in northern Shaanxi and western Inner Mongolia: Cliopatria's Sui 626 shape, which is Liang Shidu's holding

ledger.note: 628: Liang Shidu is killed and the Liang surrenders. 'Emperor Taizong deemed the time ripe and ordered his brother-in-law' Chai Shao to lead a major campaign; under Tang siege Liang Luoren killed Liang Shidu and surrendered (May or June 628).

wars.name: Tang conquest of Liang Shidu's Liang

zones.text: the Ordos and the bend of the Yellow River in northern Shaanxi and western Inner Mongolia: Cliopatria's Sui 626 shape, which is Liang Shidu's holding

wars.outcome: Tang victory: the eastern city of Shuofang fell in 622 and the whole Liang in 628, the last rival regime of the Sui collapse.
wars.note: Liang Shidu 'submitted to Eastern Turks' Shibi Khan,' who gave him the title Dadupiqie Qaghan, and the Eastern Turks occupied the Ordos with his help; in 626 he urged them to invade the Tang.

certainty.note: A steppe-edge region on the Yellow River bend; the page gives no boundary.

sources.title: Liang Shidu

sources.title: Transition from Sui to Tang

notes: REBEL STATE. Cliopatria carries this land as 'Sui Dynasty' 626-627; the Sui dossier calls those shapes wrong and names this slug. Liang Shidu submitted to Shibi Khan of the Eastern Turks, who named him Dadupiqie Qaghan: the Eastern Turks' dossier (group ia-01) should carry a vassal_start for this region with counterpart liang-shidu-s-liang; this dossier does not. The month of the 628 death differs between the two Tang histories.
